Release: individual records

release_records.Rd

The external source shared its individual records: another cohort's covariates and outcomes, subject by subject. The records must follow the design of your target and use your covariate names:

  • for a Cox target (target_cox()): z, time and event, and optionally stratum;

  • for a nested case-control target (target_ncc()): z, case and set;

  • for a discrete-time target (target_discrete()): z, interval and event, on the target's intervals, and optionally stratum.

The design is read off the arguments you give: case makes nested case-control records, interval discrete-time records, and time Cox records.

Individual records support the composite-likelihood divergence (divergence = "composite" in cv.bregsurv()): their log-likelihood is added to yours with weight \(\eta\), the two cohorts share the coefficients, and each keeps its own baseline hazard. On a Cox target they also support the Mahalanobis and Kullback-Leibler divergences, for which cv.bregsurv() fits a Cox model to the records and borrows from its coefficients and their precision.

Usage

release_records(
  z,
  time = NULL,
  event = NULL,
  stratum = NULL,
  case = NULL,
  set = NULL,
  interval = NULL
)

Arguments

z

The external covariates: a numeric matrix or data frame with one row per external subject and columns named like your covariates. Columns you do not have are ignored; a covariate of yours that the records lack is an error.

time, event

Cox records: each external subject's follow-up time (positive) and event indicator (1 = event, 0 = censored). For discrete-time records, event is the event indicator that goes with interval.

stratum

Optional strata of the external subjects (Cox or discrete-time records). The external baselines are kept apart from yours either way.

case, set

Nested case-control records: the case indicator (1 = case, 0 = control) and the matched set of each row; every set holds exactly one case. Give these instead of time.

interval

Discrete-time records: the last interval each external subject was at risk in, a whole number on the target's intervals. Give it with event, instead of time.

Value

An object of class "bregsurv_release", a list with form = "records", kind ("cohort", "ncc" or "discrete"), and the checked z, time, event, stratum, case, set and interval (those not given are NULL).

See also

cv.bregsurv(); the other releases, release_coef(), release_score(), release_model(); the targets, target_cox(), target_ncc() and target_discrete().

Examples

# Cox records, with strata
data(ExampleData_indi)
ext <- ExampleData_indi$external
release_records(ext$z, time = ext$time, event = ext$status, stratum = ext$stratum)
#> Release: individual records (Cox design), 2000 subjects, 10 strata

# nested case-control records
data(ExampleData_cc_indi)
ecc <- ExampleData_cc_indi$external
release_records(ecc$z, case = ecc$y, set = ecc$stratum)
#> Release: individual records (nested case-control design), 2500 subjects

# discrete-time records
data(ExampleData_discrete)
reg <- ExampleData_discrete$external
release_records(reg$z, interval = reg$interval, event = reg$status)
#> Release: individual records (discrete-time design), 1000 subjects
